# User Routes

This file defines the API routes for user-related operations, including fetching user data, managing connection requests, and retrieving potential matches for users.

## Overview

The `user.js` file acts as the entry point for all user-specific API endpoints within the application. It handles requests related to user profiles, connection requests, and the user feed. It leverages middleware for authentication and interacts with the `User` and `ConnectionRequestModel` to perform data operations.

<CardGroup cols={2}>
  <Card title="User Data Retrieval" icon="👤">
    Endpoints for fetching individual user profiles and listing users for the feed.
  </Card>
  <Card title="Connection Management" icon="🤝">
    Routes for viewing received connection requests and listing accepted connections.
  </Card>
</CardGroup>

## Routes

### Get User By ID

Retrieves a user's profile information based on their ID.

#### GET `/user/get-user-by-id/:userId`

<ParamField name="userId" type="string" required>
  The unique identifier for the user to retrieve.
</ParamField>

<ResponseExample>
```json 200 OK
{
  "data": {
    "_id": "60d5ec49d3e8a10015f7e2a1",
    "firstName": "Jane",
    "lastName": "Doe",
    "photoUrl": "http://example.com/photo.jpg",
    "age": 28,
    "gender": "female",
    "about": "Loves hiking and exploring new places.",
    "skills": ["hiking", "photography"],
    "email": "jane.doe@example.com"
  }
}
```

```json 404 Not Found
{
  "message": "User not found"
}
```

```json 500 Internal Server Error
{
  "message": "Server Error"
}
```
</ResponseExample>

### Get Received Connection Requests

Fetches all connection requests where the logged-in user is the recipient and the status is "interested".

#### GET `/user/requests/received`

<Info>This route requires authentication via the `userAuth` middleware.</Info>

<ResponseExample>
```json 200 OK
{
  "message": "Data fetched successfully",
  "data": [
    {
      "_id": "60d5ec49d3e8a10015f7e2a2",
      "status": "interested",
      "fromUserId": {
        "_id": "60d5ec49d3e8a10015f7e2a3",
        "firstName": "John",
        "lastName": "Smith",
        "photoUrl": "http://example.com/john.jpg",
        "age": 30,
        "gender": "male",
        "about": "Software engineer and avid gamer.",
        "skills": ["javascript", "react", "node.js"]
      }
    }
  ]
}
```
</ResponseExample>

### Get User Connections

Retrieves all accepted connection requests involving the logged-in user, either as the sender or recipient.

#### GET `/user/connections`

<Info>This route requires authentication via the `userAuth` middleware.</Info>

<ResponseExample>
```json 200 OK
{
  "data": [
    {
      "_id": "60d5ec49d3e8a10015f7e2a4",
      "status": "accepted",
      "fromUserId": {
        "_id": "60d5ec49d3e8a10015f7e2a3",
        "firstName": "John",
        "lastName": "Smith",
        "photoUrl": "http://example.com/john.jpg",
        "age": 30,
        "gender": "male",
        "about": "Software engineer and avid gamer.",
        "skills": ["javascript", "react", "node.js"]
      },
      "toUserId": {
        "_id": "60d5ec49d3e8a10015f7e2a1",
        "firstName": "Jane",
        "lastName": "Doe",
        "photoUrl": "http://example.com/photo.jpg",
        "age": 28,
        "gender": "female",
        "about": "Loves hiking and exploring new places.",
        "skills": ["hiking", "photography"]
      }
    }
  ]
}
```
</ResponseExample>

### Get User Feed

Fetches a paginated list of users that the logged-in user has not yet connected with or sent a request to.

#### GET `/user/feed`

<Info>This route requires authentication via the `userAuth` middleware.</Info>

<ParamField name="page" type="integer" default="1">
  The page number for pagination.
</ParamField>
<ParamField name="limit" type="integer" default="10">
  The maximum number of users to return per page. Maximum limit is 50.
</ParamField>

<ResponseExample>
```json 200 OK
{
  "data": [
    {
      "firstName": "Peter",
      "lastName": "Jones",
      "photoUrl": "http://example.com/peter.jpg",
      "age": 25,
      "gender": "male",
      "about": "Musician and aspiring chef.",
      "skills": ["guitar", "cooking"]
    },
    {
      "firstName": "Sarah",
      "lastName": "Lee",
      "photoUrl": "http://example.com/sarah.jpg",
      "age": 29,
      "gender": "female",
      "about": "Travel blogger and photographer.",
      "skills": ["travel", "photography", "writing"]
    }
  ]
}
```
</ResponseExample>

## Usage Example

Here's how you might use these user routes in a client application:

<CodeGroup>
```javascript JavaScript
// Example using fetch to get user connections
async function getUserConnections(token) {
  try {
    const response = await fetch("https://your-api.com/user/connections", {
      headers: {
        Authorization: `Bearer ${token}`,
      },
    });
    const data = await response.json();
    console.log("User Connections:", data.data);
    return data.data;
  } catch (error) {
    console.error("Error fetching connections:", error);
    throw error;
  }
}

// Example using fetch to get user feed
async function getUserFeed(token, page = 1, limit = 10) {
  try {
    const response = await fetch(`https://your-api.com/user/feed?page=${page}&limit=${limit}`, {
      headers: {
        Authorization: `Bearer ${token}`,
      },
    });
    const data = await response.json();
    console.log("User Feed:", data.data);
    return data.data;
  } catch (error) {
    console.error("Error fetching user feed:", error);
    throw error;
  }
}
```

```javascript Node.js
// Example using a hypothetical API client for Node.js
const apiClient = require('./apiClient'); // Assuming you have an API client

async function getUserConnections() {
  try {
    const response = await apiClient.get('/user/connections');
    console.log('User Connections:', response.data.data);
    return response.data.data;
  } catch (error) {
    console.error('Error fetching connections:', error);
    throw error;
  }
}

async function getUserFeed(page = 1, limit = 10) {
  try {
    const response = await apiClient.get('/user/feed', { params: { page, limit } });
    console.log('User Feed:', response.data.data);
    return response.data.data;
  } catch (error) {
    console.error('Error fetching user feed:', error);
    throw error;
  }
}
```
</CodeGroup>

## Common Errors / Troubleshooting

<AccordionGroup>
  <Accordion title="User Not Found when using /get-user-by-id/:userId">
    This error typically occurs when the `userId` provided in the URL does not correspond to an existing user in the database. Double-check that the `userId` is correct and that the user exists.
  </Accordion>
  <Accordion title="Server Error when fetching connections or feed">
    A "Server Error" (500) indicates an unexpected issue on the server-side. This could be due to database connection problems, unhandled exceptions in the route logic, or issues with external service integrations. Check server logs for more detailed error messages.
  </Accordion>
</AccordionGroup>
